A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Zeroth-Order Optimization at the Edge of Stability. All 38 pages support comparison, including equations, Table 1, Figures 1–13, and Appendices A–D. Appendix pages 12–38 have identical text and rendered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original neural-network training experiments on CIFAR-10 and synthetic sequence sorting, including loss trajectories, Hessian curvature measurements, and sensitivity analyses in Section 5 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and their results in Section 5 and Appendix D, including CNN, ResNet, ViT, LSTM, and Mamba training.

M1.justification: The two-point estimator, ZO-GD, ZO-GDM, ZO-Adam, and frozen-preconditioner procedures in Section 3 are unchanged. Appendix B retains the same alternative-estimator formulations.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same CIFAR-10 classification and synthetic sequence-sorting tasks. The full-batch, mini-batch, and other tested scenarios are retained without additions or removals.

E2.justification: Figure 1 retains the same empirical GD versus ZO-GD comparison. No comparison method is added, removed, or replaced in the reported experiments.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C retain identical sample sizes, preprocessing, architectures, losses, optimizer settings, and curvature-measurement procedures. No new evaluation protocol or revised experimental setting is reported.

E4.justification: The catapult, smoothing-parameter, and mini-batch analyses in Section 5.4 are unchanged. Appendix D retains the same ZO-Adam momentum sweep and empirical commutativity check.

E5.justification: Run information, statistical estimation procedures, and uncertainty reporting are unchanged. The plotted stability bands remain theoretical bounds; no seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: Figures 1–13 and their reported findings are unchanged. This includes the EoS trajectories and the relative commutator decrease from 0.8–0.9 to below 0.05 reported in Appendix D.3.

T1.justification: The definitions, propositions, stability theorems, and assumptions in Sections 3–4 are unchanged, including the commutativity assumption for Frozen ZO-Adam. Appendices A–B retain identical proofs and estimator extensions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about exact mean-square stability conditions, full-spectrum dependence, tractable curvature bounds, and empirical EoS behavior.

C2.justification: The explanations of trace-related implicit regularization, momentum, smoothing bias, and approximate commutativity are unchanged. The same full-batch scope, theoretical qualifications, and future directions remain.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures are identical, including architecture details, 50 power iterations, 500 Hutchinson probes, a single NVIDIA H100 GPU, and 50 commutator probes per checkpoint. No code or data access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the references retain the same cited works and positioning relative to earlier ZO optimization, EoS, and stability research.

P1.justification: The preprint footer is replaced by ICML 2026 proceedings and copyright wording, and the arXiv version/date is updated. Scientific prose, terminology, and section order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Main-text page and column breaks shift. Figure 5 moves from below Figure 4 in the left column to the top of the right column on page 7. Figure content, captions, table structure, and appendix layout remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 updates publication metadata and modestly reflows the main text while preserving the scientific arguments, results, proofs, and reproducibility details. These presentation changes establish no meaningful net improvement or deterioration in overall paper quality.
